candidates.title: Review translations for a technical decision record

demandEvidence.chore: Translate or review translations for a technical decision record.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I welcome constructive feedback, and welcome help with the translations.

ease.reason: A sample translation draft can be reviewed manually, but no relevant implementation reference is attached.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: a technical documentation maintainer might pay for translation review; this request establishes no buyer or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can compare drafts with human edits, but target languages and quality criteria are unspecified.

autonomy.reason: A draft can be generated repeatedly; a bilingual person must verify terminology and meaning.

evidence.reason: The request explicitly welcomes translation help, but gives no language, volume, recurrence, or result evidence.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: the request asks for translation help, but names no target languages, repeat workflow, buyer, or implementation reference. A draft with human review is conceivable; demand and usefulness remain uncorroborated.

candidates.title: Create a film look for each photo

demandEvidence.chore: Create a film look tailored to a photo.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want to help everyone (including myself) to quickly get a film look, because I think each photo has its own vibe, so one preset just can't fit them all.

ease.reason: One sample image and a chosen style could be tested, but no implementation source documents image editing capability.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: photographers might pay for tailored looks; the post establishes a product goal, not demand for a separate service.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock could produce style suggestions for sample images, but faithful image transformation is unsupported here.

autonomy.reason: An image could be processed repeatedly, but a person must judge visual quality and approve outputs.

evidence.reason: The maker describes a film-look app and its goal; the excerpt does not establish users, results, or demand for another service.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: the maker describes a film-look photo app and a goal of fitting each image, but this is a product demonstration rather than evidence of a separate paying service need. No supplied reference supports a new AI editing workflow.

candidates.title: Review store information buyers may need

demandEvidence.chore: Assess whether store information is missing that could make buyers hesitate.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Is there any missing information—such as reviews, policies, contact details, or business background—that would make you hesitate to buy?

ease.reason: A checklist can be tested on fictional storefront text, but no implementation reference supports page review.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: an online shop might pay for a completeness review; the question proves no willingness to pay.

feasibility.reason: A mock can list supplied information fields, but criteria and repeat process are unvalidated.

autonomy.reason: A draft checklist can repeat; a person must verify omissions and judge relevance.

evidence.reason: The question names possible purchase concerns, but does not establish repeated need or a review method.

candidates.reason: Below threshold and duplicate customer: an automated storefront information checklist overlaps recent post 98b4f6281cc3de4ecdfa95f6 on the specific online-shop buyer. The single question also gives no repeat-use evidence.

candidates.title: Collect customer notes before checkout

demandEvidence.chore: Allow shoppers to add special instructions or custom messages before checkout.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want to allow customers to add special instructions or custom messages before they proceed to checkout.

ease.reason: A sample form can capture fictional notes, but no supplied implementation reference documents checkout integration.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: an online shop might pay for handling order instructions; no payment or buyer commitment is shown.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can categorize supplied sample notes, but checkout access and useful categories are unverified.

autonomy.reason: Categorization can repeat, while a person must confirm meaning before any fulfillment action.

evidence.reason: The request explicitly names special instructions and custom messages before checkout, but gives no recurrence or implementation detail.

candidates.reason: Below threshold and duplicate customer: a proposed online-shop buyer overlaps recent post 98b4f6281cc3de4ecdfa95f6 on the specific online-shop customer. The request gives no implementation reference, recurring need, or validated payer.

steps.message: Assessed all ten sealed discussion assignments. Four concrete excerpts received provisional five-criterion assessments and were rejected below threshold; the other six lack a sufficiently stated chore or describe a one-off issue. No eligible nonduplicate proposal met the 6-point threshold.
